rows.why: Classic two-Bragg-ends resolution: seg 16001 falls monotonically from 360k at 16000 down to 90k at 16002 and seg 16003 rises to 145k at the 16003 end, so both prongs of this 96 cm chain get hotter going away from 16002, which is the only kink (136 deg opening) and has no competing candidate nearer than 38 cm.

A clean two-prong V at the lowest-z candidate (z=81.6), visible directly in the X-Z panel: one arm is a 43 cm 2x-MIP track that exits the x=-200 wall at 7006 so it has no Bragg, the other climbs 65k to 379k over 30 cm into the shower core at 7044, which is rule 1 for an electron shower developing away from the vertex; 7044 itself has three segments rising toward it so it is the shower core, not the vertex, and the prongs are 34 degrees apart so the collinearity trap does not fire.

Rule 1 at full strength on a degree-5 star: all three measured prongs rise away and none rises toward, an 85 cm proton (51k to 79k) that ends in a secondary hadronic star at 12002, a 29.5 cm segment climbing 52k to 149k (x2.89) that feeds the EM shower beyond 12012, and a 29.9 cm backward prong at 55k to 111k; the prong pairs sit at 31, 93 and 99 degrees so no pair is near-collinear.

Textbook rule 1 at a degree-5 vertex: nothing rises toward 22024 and three independent prongs rise away to genuine above-MIP stopping ends (22.1 cm proton to 188k at 22020, 13.8 cm proton to 113k at 22013, 11.3 cm segment to 86k at 22025), while the nearby 22018 is disqualified because seg 22040 rises toward it to 143k.

Rule 1 with a decisive profile - p4 shows seg 11003 flat at ~65k for 65 cm then spiking to 310k in the last centimetre at 11003, so the muon stops there and starts at 11002, where a short hot pi+/proton stub (127k out to 11000) also cools inward; 11002 is the only junction and the two prongs are 137 degrees apart, not collinear.

Rule 1 on the 48.8 cm heavy track: the p4 profile rises broadly and monotonically over the last ~12 cm into 200k at the 14000 end (real Bragg), while the 470k at 14002 is only a 2-point spike (vertex overlap charge, not a Bragg), so 14002 is the cool start end; it is also the lowest-z point of the track and sits ~8 cm from the low-z tip of the pi0 shower cluster 55, the expected photon-conversion gap.

I took the 4-prong hot star at 143049, where two short stopping protons (to 143050 at 205k and 143054 at 186k) both point away and no attached segment is hotter at the vertex than beyond it, but trap 3 applies hard here: the 143054/143056 prong pair is ~152 degrees apart and 143050-143049-143056-143055 forms a 26.7 cm chain hot at both free ends and cooler in the middle, so I dropped a tier; the long 82.5 cm track in cluster 7 enters at z=501 (detector face) and is screened out as a cosmic.

Rule 7 on an NC-like event: the 508 cm cluster 7 with its 233 cm Bragg-terminated track is a cosmic (screened out), and the remaining small clusters form a cone from (110,-71,220) out to (33,-87,303) whose dense core sits at z=227-240, so back-tracking one shower-max length puts the apex at ~(114,-70,216); I take 108136, the deg-3 hub of a standalone cluster right at that apex, but the pi0 photon converts away from the true vertex so the real vertex may be upstream and unmarked.

Rule 7 with rule 8 hovering: the whole event is one 16 cm object with flat ~1 MIP dQ/dx and no Bragg at either end, but two prongs leave 10000 at only ~32 degrees and the p4 profile shows a 2-MIP (85k) bump 2-3 cm from 10000, which reads as an e+e- pair overlapping at a photon conversion, so 10000 is the apex; the neutrino vertex itself is probably upstream of it and invisible.

The only substantial cluster runs boundary to boundary (one end on the anode at x=-195, the other on the bottom wall at y=-199) with flat MIP dQ/dx and no Bragg anywhere, which is my cosmic signature, and the only other charge is a dispersed fragment group with no readable direction (rule 8); I picked 5002 because it is the lowest-z candidate (z=11.4) and is a genuine ~90 degree two-prong junction with both prongs heading forward in z, but I would not be surprised to be wrong.

Rule 1 read off p4 rather than the 5 cm means: the 32.2 cm track rises monotonically 115k->230k toward the 109075 end (the final collapse to 50k is the fit overshooting the stopping point), so 109074 is the cool start; it is the lowest-z candidate at z=367.5, and the cluster-113 to cluster-15 shower axis back-extrapolates to (-20.6,-13.4,367), within a couple of cm of it.

Rule 7 with the trap-3 caution: the 33.8 cm segment is far too heavily ionizing (3-6 MIP over 34 cm) to be a proton, and p4 shows dense blobs at both its ends with a 15 cm MIP stretch between them, which reads as vertex charge at 2001, an electron travelling ~15 cm as a MIP, then showering from 2015 onward and fanning out to z=236; 2001 is the lowest-z end and the whole structure moves upward and forward in z, so it is not a downward cosmic.

Rule 1 with the two-Bragg-ends trap: seg 15009 (74 cm) climbs monotonically to 195k at 15000 and seg 15011 climbs to 179k at 15007, so both heavy prongs stop away from 15006, and its cone profile is the only monotone one (far-near +16.6 cm); the EM spray hanging off 15004 6.7 cm downstream reads as a displaced photon conversion, but 15004 is a real competitor so not certain.

The event is a V whose apex sits at 13002/13006; I broke that 2.3 cm tie with the trap-3 collinearity check - at 13006 the pi+ stub and the 9.9 cm proton leave at 163 deg (nearly one straight line) whereas at 13002 the three prongs are mutually 52/71/74 deg, a genuine fan, and 13002 is also the lowest-z candidate in the cluster; 13019 is rejected because 3 of its 4 segments rise toward it.

Only one real object, a 120 cm track; rule 1 picks the cool end because the 5 cm mean is 118600 at 18000 against 69082 at 18002 and the profile decays over ~8 cm from the 18000 end, so 18000 is the stopping end - 18002 is also the low-z end and neither end sits on a wall, but a single flat-MIP track with no second prong leaves cosmic contamination possible.

Rule 1 plus the multi-prong star: five prongs radiate from 60040 at mutual angles of 72-102 deg, including two short heavy stubs (109k over 3.8 cm, 112k over 1.8 cm) and an 8.3 cm prong Bragg-stopping at 60029 (161k); the trap-3 test eliminates the 5.5 cm competitor 60038, where the 140 cm muon and the link back to 60040 leave at 175.6 deg, i.e. 60038 is a break point inside the muon, so I read the hot 7.6 cm link as vertex-region pile-up on the muon's first centimetres.

Rule 1 on a two-ended track: seg 4002 rises from 59311 at 4001 to 89264/120696 at the 4000 end, so the particle stops there and 4001 is the start; 4001 is also the lowest-z candidate, but it sits exactly on the x = -200 anode wall and the event is a single horizontal track at y = 110 with no second prong, so this is very likely an entering cosmic rather than a neutrino.

Rule 1 puts two real Bragg profiles pointing away from 5004 - seg 5006 climbs 73k to 185k stopping at 5002 and seg 5007 climbs 101k to 215k stopping at 5005 - but trap 3 fires: the 80 cm flat-MIP prong and the 19.8 cm pi+ leave 5004 at 155 deg and the dQ/dx along that line is monotone 42881 -> 61297 | 73104 -> 130862, i.e. it also reads as one muon entering at the z=497 wall and stopping at 5002, which drops this a tier; the 26.3 cm proton at 78 deg to both still needs a real interaction here.

Rule 1 read on a tiny event: the 36 cm track is flat MIP (57k-63k) and heads forward in +z to exit near z = 500, while a 3.3 cm stub uniformly at 167572 (4x MIP) hangs off 6003 as a short stopping proton, making 6003 the junction; 6004 is only 2.6 cm away but is the degree-1 far end of that stub.

I can tell three stories and cannot separate them, so I let the ranked rules decide the 2.6 cm split: rule 1 is mildly negative at 12002 (the 56 cm track and the 6.5 cm link are both hotter AT it) and neutral at the 12003 three-prong fan (90/126/144 deg, no collinearity), and rule 2 also favours 12003 by 1.8 cm in z; against that, the 190k charge concentration sits at 12002, and the whole cluster reads equally well as a cosmic entering at z = 497 and stopping at 12002 with a Michel fan at 12003 (rule 3), which is why this is unclear. Cluster 88+89 was rejected as a candidate host because it is a straight line in the principal frame.

Rule 1 on the only substantial object: seg 14002 rises from 59147 at 14001 to 93568 at 14002 with a further 4.5 cm stub at 113066, so the particle stops at 14002/14000 and 14001 is the cool start, and 14001 is also by far the lowest-z candidate (z = 4.7); it sits in the cathode/upstream corner though, so an entering particle is quite possible.

Rule 1 forces the choice between the only two real candidates: seg 12000 rises from 48745 at 12000 to 89350 at 12001, and the small fragment clusters 28/29/30/31 sit 14-17 cm from 12001 like a Michel/delta spray, so 12001 is the stopping end (rule 3) and 12000 is the start - but 12000 lies on the z = 500 downstream wall, so this is an entering backward track with no neutrino signature.

Rules 6/7 plus rule 1 agree: back-projecting the cluster-110 chain and the 23.9 cm cluster-13 shower stem both lands within a few cm of (26,155,140), and the 38 cm proton seg 18022 rises 108990 to 187167 stopping away at 18019, with the zoom showing 18020 as the extreme upstream apex of the whole fan; the residual doubt is purely which of the three sub-cm-separated ids (18020/18018/18096) is meant, and I chose the one the 38 cm segment attaches to.

Rule 1 rules out the stopping-cosmic reading: the 112 cm track is cooler at 2002 (51868) than at its far end, so it does not stop here, which means the 3.5 cm stub at 148572 is a separate short proton and 2002 is a three-prong junction; I held back from certain because the entire event hugs the x = -197 anode wall and the long track exits at the z = 500 / y = -192 corner.

Travel direction decided it rather than the raw rule-1 count: the 25.7 cm pion seg 9011 is MIP at 9003 and rises to about 100k approaching 9006, so it moves 9003 to 9006 and 9006 is a secondary hadronic star (proton Bragg to 280k at 9004 plus a second pion Bragg at 9007), while the 360 cm muon leaves 9003 forward and exits at z=500 with no monotone Bragg at the 9003 end, and the cluster-49 EM shower apex sits 8 cm away like a gamma conversion off the same vertex.

Rule 1 on the only fitted object: the 7.5 cm proton is 232k at 14000 and cooler 178k at 14001, so it stops at 14000 and starts at 14001, where a second 0.5 cm proton stub also attaches; I held back from certain because the surrounding event is a 60 cm wide cloud of sub-centimetre blips with no readable structure (heuristic 8) that could equally hide the true vertex.

Geometry decided it: the two real prongs, a 43.7 cm muon to 15001 and a 32 cm low-charge track to 15000, both terminate on the z=500 downstream wall and meet in a clean V whose apex is at z=480.7, so nothing in the event is upstream of that apex; 15002/15004/15009 are the same physical point within 1 cm and I took 15004 because it sits on the apex and holds the muon, which is also why I did not call it certain.

Read as an NC pi0: rule 1 puts the 13.1 cm heavily-ionising cluster-70 track leaving 70078 and Bragging to 138k at 70079, and that track is at 98 degrees to seg 21035 so it is a genuine separate prong and not a broken continuation; shower cluster 21 peaks at 124k (about 3x MIP, an e+e- overlap) at 21001 only 3.7 cm away and the second shower back-extrapolates from 75092 to within 16 degrees of the same spot, and since a proton cannot travel before depositing I put the vertex at the proton start rather than at the conversion point.

Rule 1 on a single 434 cm track: p4 shows a textbook monotone Bragg at the far end 3000 (190k falling to MIP within 5 cm on the stopping-muon template) and plain MIP at 3004, which also carries two short stubs (1.9 cm at 120k and 2.0 cm at 66k) that read as hadronic recoil; the hot patch at the 3002 junction is only 1-2 cm wide and is a blob, not a Bragg shape, so it does not compete, and I stopped short of certain because at z=9.5 an entering muon would look the same.

I could not find an interaction point at all: clusters 17 and 24 are one track that enters at the z=0.1 face with flat MIP (no Bragg at 17001) and stops 280 cm later where seg 24005 climbs to 160k and seg 24007 falls 156k to 18k with a Michel-like 3.4 cm 9k hook, which rule 3 says is never the vertex, while the 17002 kink is a 163 degree back-to-back pair (the collinearity trap) and cluster 25 is a second track entering at z=1.9 and stopping; 17001 is only my best guess as the candidate nearest a vertex that lies upstream of the front face.

The 4.1 cm and 9.7 cm pion pieces are one continuous hadron running 1008 to 1003 to 1000 and Bragging to 143k at 1000, which makes 1003 an internal kink rather than a junction; 1008 is where that hadron and the 26.8 cm flat-MIP track actually meet, at 122 degrees, and that track stays flat because it exits the y=-200 wall at 1001, so rule 1 is satisfied at 1008, which is also the lowest-z candidate.

Nearly nothing to work with: the only fitted object is a 23.9 cm flat 1.4x-MIP track whose 14000 end sits on the z=500 wall, so by elimination its interior end 14001 must be the origin, but neither end has a Bragg so rule 1 gives no real signal, and three unexplained sub-centimetre blips at z=451, 459 and 467 lie further upstream on roughly the same axis and could just as well mark the true vertex.

Rule 1 names 7007 and nothing else does: it is the only vertex in the event with a segment rising away (the 26.5 cm track climbing 62k to a 102k stop at 7000) and none rising toward it. Two things pull my confidence right down to guessing: the prong pair at 7007 is 160 degrees, so this may be one scattered particle rather than a junction, and the 5.6 cm chain on the other side runs out at y=198.3, within 2 cm of the top wall, which would make the whole 32 cm object an entering particle that simply stops, with the real origin outside the detector near 7001.

The zoom at half-width 8/16 shows a ~52 degree kink at 108102 between two heavy prongs (a 5.3 cm proton at ~105k toward 108100 and a 6.2 cm proton rising to 161k Bragg at 108101), sitting at the most upstream tip of the event with the EM shower apex 13001 about 7 cm downstream as a displaced gamma conversion; but 108100 and 13001 are both within 10 cm and I could not separate them cleanly, so this is close to a guess between three ids in the same region.

Rule 1 is perfect here - p4 shows two independent, template-following Bragg peaks pointing away from 9002: the 8.2 cm proton falls from 250k at 9000 to about 30k at 9002, and the 32.3 cm muon leaves 9002 at about 60k and climbs to 140k at 9001, and there is no other junction in the event; but the two prongs leave 9002 at about 163 degrees, so I drop one tier for the collinearity trap.

Rule 1 plus rule 2: p4 shows seg 28078 flat at ~80k for 45 cm then climbing to 300k at 28059, so its start end 28058 (z=168) is the most upstream free end in the event, and the dense many-prong cluster 19 begins only 6 cm downstream at 19001 with a 2 MIP segment, which reads as a gamma converting just past the vertex; 19001 is the competing pick 6 cm away.

Rule 3 settles it - the 20.4 cm muon on 21038 is hotter at 21037 with a short 8+9.5 cm electron chain hanging off that same end, so 21037 is the stopping/Michel end and 21038 is the vertex end; 21038 is also a degree-4 junction at the lowest z (40.6) whose 75 cm prong leaves at 38k and only reaches 87k where it stars into protons at 21041, and the whole 69/13/64 shower spray lies along one ray from 21038.

Rule 1 on the one clean track: the 23.8 cm proton climbs from 110k at 94055 to a 225k Bragg at 94056, so 94055 is its start and the most upstream point of the event, and the zoom shows the shower cluster 18 beginning 6.6 cm downstream at 18001 with a 92k (2 MIP) pair-like segment, off the proton's line - a displaced conversion rather than the vertex; 18001 is the competing candidate.

This is one straight 36 cm line sitting 4 cm off the anode at x=-196 that has been fitted with two or three overlapping duplicate segments - the same low-z end reads 213893 on seg 5009 and 11847 on seg 5006 - so the dQ/dx evidence contradicts itself and rule 1 cannot be trusted; I take the low-z end 5004 because it is the only vertex with nothing rising toward it and rule 2 favours it, but I am close to guessing.

Rule 1 gives 19001 two of two prongs rising away and none toward, and the zoom at half-width 12 shows the fan of tracks radiating from that point; the 17.4 cm muon of cluster 94 also starts 6 cm away at 94126 and stops at 94128 (rule 3), which corroborates the region, but 92119 sits only 5.2 cm away carrying the 59 cm exiting muon and I cannot separate the two ids.

Rule 1 fixes the apex of a 364 cm one-cluster shower: 12001/12006 (0.6 cm apart) is the lowest-z point at z=406, seg 12098 leaving 12006 rises from 52k to 132k as it enters the shower, and everything downstream of z=420 fans away from that tip with nothing rising toward it; only one prong is directionally informative though, since the 11 cm proton stub to 12016 sits at 3 MIP at both ends and says nothing about direction.

Rule 1: the only real object is a 9.2 cm proton whose dQ/dx climbs monotonically along the proton template from 100k at 21001 to 310k at 21000, so it stops at 21000 and starts at 21001, which additionally carries a second 2.1 cm prong and is the lower-z end.

Rule 1 satisfied on both prongs at 12006: a 15.6 cm proton rises away x1.54 to a Bragg at 12001 and a 13.1 cm electron rises away x2.39 (42k at the start, shower-like 102k downstream), the two leaving at 87 degrees so this is not a collinear scatter, and 12006 is the lowest-z candidate in the event.

Rule 1 at the deg-3 hub 12117: a 30.9 cm proton rises away x1.81 into a Bragg at 12001 and, through the 0.8 cm link to 12002 (0.7 cm away, so I take the higher-degree junction), a 15.3 cm electron rises away x3.83 into a 297k shower core; this junction is the lowest-z point of the event and the overview shows the shower fanning out downstream from exactly here.

Rule 1 with all three prongs non-decreasing away from 5009: a 10.8 cm proton 113k->141k, a 17.9 cm electron 49k->93k (x1.90, the classic MIP-start-then-shower), and a 4.6 cm stub, with the proton and electron 94 degrees apart; 5009 at z=19.7 is the most upstream candidate in the event and the rest of the shower marches downstream to z=169.

Rule 1 perfect at 16013: an 84.7 cm track rises away x2.36 into a 178k Bragg at 16001 and a 27.4 cm electron rises away x4.81 into a 272k shower core at 16043, the two prongs 117 degrees apart, and 16013 at z=300.9 is the most upstream candidate in the whole event.

Rule 1 plus rule 2 at the apex of the V seen in X-Z: the 87.9 cm track cools toward 15003 (72k here vs 101k at its far end 15002, where it stops and knocks out a 7.1 cm 212k proton, i.e. a hadronic interaction, not the vertex), the whole shower blob fans out from 15003 to higher z, and 15003 at z=95.8 is the lowest-z candidate.

Rule 1 with both prongs rising away from 19006: a 10.2 cm proton 139k->211k stopping at 19019 and a 22.2 cm electron 69k->155k developing into the shower, 93 degrees apart, and 19006 at z=29.8 is the most upstream candidate in the event with the whole 484 cm shower cluster spreading downstream of it.

Rule 1 at the apex of the clean V in X-Z: both prongs are non-decreasing away from 5007 (the 80 cm track 74k->99k, which then interacts at 5001 producing the separate 6.5 cm 173k proton of cluster 96 three cm away, and the 15.8 cm shower prong 78k->83k), they leave 97 degrees apart, and 5007 at z=367.7 is the most upstream point of the event.

Two clean Bragg profiles point away from 11002 - seg 11003 sits flat at MIP for 22 cm then climbs to 150k at 11003, and seg 11018 climbs to 145k at 11010 - so it is hot at both far ends and cool at the junction, which rules out the single-scattered-particle reading of the 146 deg prong pair; the stub fan at 11004 on the muon's stopping end is a Michel (rule 3, far end), and 11007 with its two short protons is 14 cm away.

Rule 1 at its cleanest, and the p4 shape confirms it is a Bragg and not a hot blob: seg 12007 climbs smoothly along the proton template from 90k at 12002 to 300k at 12003, a 25 cm proton stopping away from 12002, while the other prong is a 289 cm flat-MIP muon that runs through 12004 and exits at the x = 200 wall; the fragments within 12 cm (clusters 56/59/35) are flat-MIP degree-1 pieces with no vertex evidence of their own.

Rule 1 decided it: the 39.5 cm proton seg 20035 is coolest (87k) at 20006 and climbs monotonically along the p4 proton template to a 215k/300k Bragg at 20007, and seg 20036 also gets hotter going away toward the shower at 20008, so both real prongs point away from 20006; the two prongs leave at about 67 degrees so the collinear-kink trap does not apply, and 20006 is the lowest-z point of cluster 20.

Rules 1 and 3: the only real object is a 258 cm muon whose 18000 end shows a textbook monotone Bragg in p4 (165k falling to MIP over the last 5 cm, hugging the stopping-muon template) while the 18002 end is flat MIP and carries a 3.3 cm 162k proton-like stub, so the muon starts at 18002, which is interior and points forward in +z rather than being a wall entry.

The strongest possible rule-1 reading: a degree-5 vertex where 4 of the 5 attached segments rise away and not one rises toward it, with three short protons Bragging at 180k, 206k and 156k at their far ends and a 40.1 cm muon climbing 41k to 129k (x3.14) to its own stopping point, which is a hadronic star that cannot be anything but an interaction point.

1005 is the apex of the whole event: the X-Z panel shows every cluster (1 at z=346-389, 80 at z=392-410, then 83, 85 and 58 out to z=443) fanning downstream from this one point, and rule 1 holds there with a 6.5 cm 157k-to-198k proton stopping at 1010 and a 23.7 cm segment climbing 70k to 174k (x2.49) into the shower, with nothing rising toward it; the prongs are 57 degrees apart.

Rule 1 at full strength: 4007 is a degree-5 junction with zero prongs rising toward it, and p4 shows both proton prongs (seg 4112 and seg 4073) climbing monotonically along the proton template to 195k and 220k e/cm at their far free ends 4011 and 4012, while the 27 cm electron leaves it toward the big EM shower that opens out downstream; it is also the low-z apex (z=211) of the 325 cm cluster.

Rule 1 with no violations at a degree-4 vertex: every informative prong at 11001 cools toward it (the 7.4 cm proton peaks at 185k at 11005, the 6.5 cm mu at 104k at 11004, the 38.7 cm segment rises away to 11020), and P2 shows it as the apex at z=378 from which the whole shower spray at z=420-458 fans forward.

Rule 1 on the only junction in a 22 cm event: a 3.6 cm proton stub at 151k (3.5 MIP throughout, so near-stopping over its whole length) hangs off 14002 toward 14001, and an 18.6 cm MIP-level track leaves the same point and exits at z=498 - a proton plus a minimum-ionising prong from a common point is the signature, and neither free end can be the vertex.

Rule 1 as strongly as it gets: 3004 is degree 5 with zero prongs rising toward it and four long prongs all cooling into it - a 152 cm muon leaving at exactly MIP (44k) and rising to 83k, a 38 cm proton to 110k, a 32 cm pion to 118k and a 38 cm electron to 81k that hands off to the cluster-70 shower 3 cm further on.

Rule 1 at the upstream apex: 19006 is degree 3 at z=358, the most upstream real vertex in the event, with nothing rising toward it - a 14 cm proton running out to a 170k (4 MIP) Bragg at 19013 and a 22.2 cm electron leaving at 66k and rising to 95k as it feeds the 268 cm shower that fans out over z=377-427.
